recipes.name: Nmap ping sweep
recipes.what: Find live hosts with ICMP echo plus TCP SYN/ACK probes, no port scan.
recipes.when: First step on a new subnet.
recipes.notes: -sn host discovery only; -PE ICMP echo; -PS/-PA TCP SYN/ACK ping ports. On the local segment nmap uses ARP automatically.

recipes.name: ARP scan
recipes.what: ARP-sweep a range on your own segment and list IP, MAC and vendor.
recipes.when: The target range is on the box's own L2 segment; the most reliable discovery there.
recipes.notes: --interface picks the NIC; the range is the engagement range you enter (not --localnet, which could reach past scope).

recipes.name: List targets (no packets)
recipes.what: Expand a CIDR and reverse-resolve names without touching the targets.
recipes.notes: -sL list scan sends only DNS queries; -R forces reverse DNS.

recipes.name: fping sweep
recipes.what: Fast ICMP sweep that prints only responding hosts.
recipes.when: Quick alive-list to feed other tools.
recipes.notes: -a show alive only; -g generate targets from CIDR.

recipes.name: Netdiscover passive ARP listen
recipes.what: Listen for ARP traffic to learn hosts without transmitting.
recipes.notes: -p passive (no ARP requests); -P parseable output; timeout bounds the run.

recipes.name: Quick top-100 TCP
recipes.what: Fast scan of nmap's 100 most common TCP ports.
recipes.when: Fast first look at a host or small range.
recipes.notes: -F top 100 ports; --open only open ports; -T4 faster timing.

recipes.name: Top-1000 TCP SYN
recipes.what: Default nmap SYN scan of the 1000 most common TCP ports.
recipes.notes: -sS half-open scan; default port set is the top 1000.

recipes.name: Full TCP 1-65535
recipes.what: Scan all TCP ports on one host.
recipes.when: Thorough follow-up on a single host.
recipes.notes: -p- all ports; --min-rate 1000 packets/sec floor (lower it on fragile links).

recipes.name: UDP top 100
recipes.what: Scan the 100 most common UDP ports.
recipes.when: Looking for DNS, SNMP, NTP, TFTP and similar.
recipes.notes: UDP is slow; open|filtered stays ambiguous until -sV.

recipes.name: Low-and-slow SYN scan
recipes.what: SYN scan with polite timing and few retries to reduce noise.
recipes.notes: -T2 polite; --scan-delay between probes; -Pn skips host discovery.

recipes.name: TCP connect scan (no root)
recipes.what: Full-connect scan that works without raw sockets.
recipes.notes: -sT uses the OS connect(); noisier in target logs than -sS.

recipes.name: Version detection on ports
recipes.what: Probe open ports to identify service and version.
recipes.when: After a port scan, with the open ports.
recipes.notes: -sV service/version; intensity 0-9 (default 7).

recipes.name: OS fingerprint
recipes.what: TCP/IP stack OS detection.
recipes.when: You need an OS guess for a host.
recipes.notes: Best with at least one open and one closed port in the list.

recipes.name: Aggressive scan (-A)
recipes.what: Version, OS, default scripts and traceroute in one pass.
recipes.notes: -A = -sV -O -sC --traceroute.

recipes.name: Default scripts
recipes.what: Run the NSE default category on chosen ports.
recipes.when: Cheap extra info after a port scan.
recipes.notes: -sC is --script=default.

recipes.name: Safe scripts
recipes.what: Run the NSE safe category (non-intrusive).
recipes.notes: Scripts in 'safe' shouldn't crash services or exploit anything.

recipes.name: Discovery scripts
recipes.what: Run the NSE discovery category.
recipes.when: Learn more about network and service details.
recipes.notes: Some make many queries (DNS, SMB, HTTP); keep the port list short.

recipes.name: Vuln-check scripts (flagged)
recipes.what: Run NSE vuln-check scripts for known issues. Some are intrusive and can upset fragile services.
recipes.when: Lab targets where you accept active checks.
recipes.notes: The vuln category includes intrusive checks (e.g. DoS-style tests). Use only on lab hosts you're fine disturbing; it checks, it doesn't exploit. For a gentler pass use Safe scripts.

recipes.name: WhatWeb fingerprint
recipes.what: Identify web server, CMS, frameworks and headers.
recipes.when: First look at any http(s) service.
recipes.notes: -a 1 single request; -a 3 probes more.

recipes.name: Response headers
recipes.what: Fetch headers, following redirects; check banner and security headers.
recipes.notes: -k ignore TLS errors; -I HEAD. Doesn't follow redirects, so it never leaves the host you entered.

recipes.name: robots.txt and sitemap
recipes.what: Download robots.txt and sitemap.xml.
recipes.when: Content hints before any directory discovery.
recipes.notes: Enter the URL without a trailing slash. Files may be empty or a 404 page.

recipes.name: Nikto scan
recipes.what: Check for common web misconfigurations and outdated components.
recipes.when: Lab web target where scanner traffic is fine.
recipes.notes: Noisy; sends many requests.

recipes.name: feroxbuster content discovery
recipes.what: Recursive directory and file discovery.
recipes.when: Mapping a web app's visible paths.
recipes.notes: -k skip TLS verify; -t threads; -d recursion depth.

recipes.name: gobuster dir
recipes.what: Directory discovery with a chosen wordlist.
recipes.notes: -k skip TLS verification.

recipes.name: testssl TLS audit
recipes.what: Test TLS protocols, ciphers, certificate and known TLS flaws.
recipes.notes: Kali installs it as testssl.

recipes.name: SMB info scripts
recipes.what: Query OS, SMB versions and signing without credentials.
recipes.notes: Informational scripts only.

recipes.name: NetExec SMB sweep
recipes.what: Hostnames, domain, OS and SMB signing across a range.
recipes.when: Mapping the Windows hosts on a network.
recipes.notes: No credentials. Also installed as nxc.

recipes.name: Share list (null session)
recipes.what: List shares anonymously.
recipes.when: Check whether a null session lists shares.
recipes.notes: -N no password. A refusal is a useful result.

recipes.name: NetExec null-session shares
recipes.what: Check shares via a null session across a range.
recipes.when: Cross-check the smbclient result on many hosts.
recipes.notes: Empty user and password, one attempt per host. Not a password spray. Tries one empty/default login only; not a guessing attack.

recipes.name: enum4linux-ng
recipes.what: Unauthenticated SMB/RPC/LDAP enumeration of users, groups, shares and policy.
recipes.notes: -A all simple checks; -oA writes JSON and YAML.

recipes.name: LDAP anonymous rootDSE
recipes.what: Read the RootDSE anonymously for naming contexts and DC info.
recipes.cmd: ldapsearch -x -H ldap://{host} -s base -b '' -LLL namingContexts defaultNamingContext dnsHostName domainFunctionality | tee {outdir}/ldap-rootdse.txt
recipes.notes: -x anonymous simple bind; base search on the empty DN returns RootDSE.

recipes.name: rpcclient null session
recipes.what: Query server and domain info over RPC with no credentials.
recipes.notes: Anonymous bind; most modern hosts refuse.

recipes.name: NetBIOS name scan
recipes.what: Retrieve NetBIOS names across a range.
recipes.notes: -r uses local UDP port 137 (needs root).

recipes.name: Core record lookup
recipes.what: Ask a lab DNS server for A, AAAA, MX, NS, TXT and SOA records.
recipes.cmd: for t in A AAAA MX NS TXT SOA; do dig @{host} +noall +answer {domain} $t; done | tee {outdir}/dns-records.txt
recipes.notes: Host = the lab DNS server. +noall +answer prints only answers.

recipes.name: Zone transfer attempt
recipes.what: Try an AXFR against the lab DNS server.
recipes.when: Lab domain where transfer testing is allowed.
recipes.notes: A refusal is the expected answer from a healthy server.

recipes.name: dnsrecon standard
recipes.what: SOA, NS, MX, A, SRV and a zone-transfer check against the lab DNS server.
recipes.notes: -n pins the name server to the lab host; -t std includes an AXFR attempt.

recipes.name: Reverse lookups for a range
recipes.what: PTR lookups for every address in a range.
recipes.notes: Only PTR queries to your resolver.

recipes.name: snmpwalk public
recipes.what: Walk the MIB with the default 'public' community.
recipes.notes: Output is large; try -v1 if v2c times out. Tries one empty/default login only; not a guessing attack.

recipes.name: SNMP info scripts
recipes.what: Pull sysDescr and device info via SNMP.
recipes.notes: Uses default community strings only.

recipes.name: ssh-audit
recipes.what: Audit SSH banner, key exchange, ciphers and host keys.
recipes.notes: Protocol negotiation only, no login attempts.

recipes.name: FTP anonymous check
recipes.what: Check whether anonymous FTP login is allowed.
recipes.notes: ftp-anon tries the anonymous user once.

recipes.name: RDP security and NTLM info
recipes.what: RDP encryption/security layers and NTLM host info.
recipes.notes: rdp-ntlm-info shows hostname/domain without credentials.

recipes.name: VNC info
recipes.what: Identify VNC version and auth types.
recipes.notes: Enter the VNC ports, e.g. 5900,5901.

recipes.name: SMTP capabilities
recipes.what: List SMTP commands and NTLM info.
recipes.notes: Doesn't enumerate users.

recipes.name: iw scan
recipes.what: List nearby access points with channel, signal and security.
recipes.notes: Sends probe requests. Use airodump-ng or Kismet to stay fully passive. Your adapter sends probe requests (normal Wi-Fi scanning).

recipes.name: Start monitor mode
recipes.what: Put the Alfa into monitor mode.
recipes.notes: Usually creates <wlan>mon. Doesn't stop NetworkManager unless you run 'airmon-ng check kill'.

recipes.name: Stop monitor mode
recipes.what: Return the adapter to managed mode.
recipes.notes: Give the monitor interface name.

recipes.name: airodump-ng all channels
recipes.what: Passively survey access points and clients on 2.4 and 5 GHz.
recipes.notes: --band abg covers both bands; -w output prefix.

recipes.name: airodump-ng one channel
recipes.what: Capture one channel for full coverage of it.
recipes.when: Focus on a specific access point's channel.
recipes.notes: -c locks the channel.

recipes.name: Kismet survey
recipes.what: Run Kismet on the monitor interface for a set time (uses GPS if gpsd has a fix).
recipes.when: Longer survey or wardrive, with the web UI.
recipes.notes: -c source; -p log folder; -t log title. Web UI at http://localhost:2501.

recipes.name: bluetoothctl scan
recipes.what: Scan for nearby classic and BLE devices.
recipes.notes: Uses the default adapter; btmgmt lets you pick one.

recipes.name: btmgmt find
recipes.what: Inquiry plus LE scan with RSSI and flags.
recipes.when: Alternative scan on a chosen adapter.
recipes.notes: Add -l for LE only, -b for classic only.

recipes.name: Classic inquiry (hcitool)
recipes.what: Classic Bluetooth inquiry listing names.
recipes.notes: May be missing on newer installs; prefer bluetoothctl or btmgmt.

recipes.name: BLE scan (hcitool)
recipes.what: BLE advertisement scan.
recipes.notes: Add --duplicates to see repeated adverts.

recipes.name: SDP service browse
recipes.what: List SDP services on a classic device.
recipes.when: After finding a classic device you own.
recipes.notes: Connects to the device, so it must be on your Mine tab. sdptool is deprecated.

recipes.name: Read GATT of a device
recipes.what: Connect and list GATT services and characteristics.
recipes.when: Inspect one BLE device you own.
recipes.cmd:
(printf 'connect %s
' {bdaddr}; sleep 8; printf 'menu gatt
list-attributes %s
back
disconnect %s
quit
' {bdaddr} {bdaddr}; sleep 2) | bluetoothctl | tee {outdir}/gatt.txt
recipes.notes: Read-only listing; fails if pairing is required. Never writes characteristics.

recipes.name: HCI capture (btmon)
recipes.what: Capture all HCI traffic from local adapters to a btsnoop file.
recipes.notes: Open the btsnoop file in Wireshark.

recipes.name: Sniffle advertising capture
recipes.what: Sniff BLE advertisements to pcap with the CC2652P.
recipes.notes: -a advertising only; -o pcap. Add -c 37|38|39 to pin a channel, -e for extended adverts. Assumes the Sniffle dongle is /dev/ttyUSB0 and Sniffle is in /opt/sniffle (setup puts it there); check with ls /dev/ttyUSB*.

recipes.name: Sniffle one device
recipes.what: Capture adverts from one advertiser address.
recipes.notes: -m filters by advertiser MAC; add -r -70 to drop weak signals. Assumes the Sniffle dongle is /dev/ttyUSB0 and Sniffle is in /opt/sniffle (setup puts it there); check with ls /dev/ttyUSB*.

recipes.name: rtl_433 decode
recipes.what: Decode ISM-band sensor transmissions to JSON.
recipes.notes: -f centre frequency; -T run time; -F json:file output.

recipes.name: rtl_power sweep 400-470 MHz
recipes.what: Wideband power sweep to CSV.
recipes.notes: -f lower:upper:bin; -i integration; -e exit time; -g gain.

recipes.name: ADS-B aircraft (readsb)
recipes.what: Receive 1090 MHz ADS-B aircraft data.
recipes.notes: Stop the dashboard's plane tracker first if it's using the dongle.

recipes.name: RTL-SDR health check
recipes.what: Confirm the dongle is detected and stable.
recipes.notes: -t tests tuner range and gains.

recipes.name: tcpdump ring buffer
recipes.what: Capture packets to rotating pcap files.
recipes.when: Long capture with bounded disk use.
recipes.notes: -C 100 MB per file; -W 10 files; -nn no name lookups.

recipes.name: tcpdump one host
recipes.what: Capture traffic to or from one host.
recipes.notes: BPF filter 'host'.

recipes.name: tshark ring buffer
recipes.what: Capture with the Wireshark engine into rotating files.
recipes.when: A capture you'll open in Wireshark.
recipes.notes: -a stop condition; -b ring buffer (size in kB).

recipes.name: Interfaces and addresses
recipes.what: Show interface addresses and link state.
recipes.notes: -br brief output.

recipes.name: Routes and neighbours
recipes.what: IPv4/IPv6 routes and ARP/ND neighbours.
recipes.when: Understand the gateway and nearby hosts.
recipes.cmd: (ip route; ip -6 route; ip neigh) | tee {outdir}/ip-route.txt

recipes.name: NetworkManager status
recipes.what: Device status and visible Wi-Fi networks.
recipes.cmd: (nmcli device status; nmcli device wifi list) | tee {outdir}/nmcli.txt
recipes.notes: The wifi list triggers a scan. Your adapter sends probe requests (normal Wi-Fi scanning).

recipes.name: USB device tree
recipes.what: List attached USB devices.
recipes.notes: -t tree view with drivers.

recipes.name: Bluetooth adapter info
recipes.what: Show the adapter's state and capabilities.
recipes.notes: Address, supported and current settings.

recipes.name: GPS fix check
recipes.what: Read a few GPS messages from gpsd.
recipes.when: Before wardriving or Kismet GPS logging.
recipes.notes: Look for TPV with mode 2 or 3.

chains.name: New network triage
chains.what: Box baseline, find hosts, quick ports, versions, then fingerprint one web service.

chains.name: Windows host enum
chains.what: Unauthenticated enumeration of one Windows/AD host.

chains.name: Web app first look
chains.what: Fingerprint and map one web service.

chains.name: Lab DNS recon
chains.what: Records, dnsrecon and a zone-transfer check against the lab DNS server.

chains.name: BLE survey
chains.what: Check the radios, scan, capture adverts, then read a device you own.

chains.name: Wi-Fi survey
chains.what: Passive survey with logging; monitor mode is switched off at the end.

chains.name: RF receive survey
chains.what: Check the SDR, sweep UHF, then decode ISM sensors.

chains.name: Service deep-dive
chains.what: All TCP ports, versions, OS, then safe scripts and common service checks.
